rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, the dominant uncertainty is the absolute performance level of this task and the contribution of each design axis. Config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most interpretable RNA-only baseline: PCA is a well-understood linear encoder and singleprofile removes all aggregation/fusion confounds. Establishing this floor is the single most informative first step because (1) it anchors every subsequent comparison—without it, a multimodal or multiprofile result cannot be attributed to a specific design choice; (2) it isolates the RNA signal quality and the task difficulty, which are the two variables that gate all downstream decisions; and (3) it is computationally cheap, preserving budget for the follow-up experiments (image-only baseline, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion) that will follow logically once the RNA floor is known. No other single experiment reduces as much uncertainty about the most fundamental question: 'how well can RNA alone solve this task with a minimal pipeline?'

Evidence: Only one experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) has been completed, yielding ~48.5% accuracy. This gives us almost no information about which design dimensions matter. The most fundamental question for a multimodal cellular profiling study is whether adding the image modality provides any benefit over RNA-only. Question: Does multimodal fusion (adding resnet50 image features via concat) improve validation accuracy over the RNA-only baseline? config_016 keeps the RNA side identical to config_001 (pca_n2000, singleprofile) and adds the simplest, most standard image setup (resnet50, concat fusion), cleanly isolating the effect of the image modality. Why this is the best next step: With only one data point, the highest-uncertainty decision is whether multimodal is worth pursuing at all. A positive result justifies investing remaining budget in fusion strategies, image encoder choices, and multiprofile aggregation within the multimodal space. A negative result redirects effort toward RNA-encoder and profile-setting improvements. No other single experiment reduces uncertainty about this pivotal design choice as efficiently.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.5266 accuracy, a clear +4.2% gain over the RNA-only baseline (config_001, 0.4849), confirming that adding image features via concat fusion is beneficial. Uncertainty: We have no information on whether multiprofile (with an aggregation step) adds further value on top of the multimodal gain, or whether singleprofile is already sufficient. Question: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) isolates the multiprofile dimension while keeping the proven multimodal+resnet50+concat backbone. Why best next: It is the most informative single experiment because a positive result opens the entire multiprofile+aggregation subspace (transformer aggregation, other encoders) for further exploitation, while a negative result confirms singleprofile sufficiency and redirects budget toward RNA/image encoder or fusion-strategy variations. It directly extends the strongest configuration with one new variable, maximizing information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieved the best result (acc=0.619, F1=0.610), showing a large gain over the singleprofile baseline (config_016, acc=0.527). This jump was driven by the multiprofile+avgpool combination, but we have not yet tested whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) can further improve over simple average pooling. Question: config_020 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) identical to the current best. This is a clean single-variable test of whether the aggregation strategy is at its ceiling or whether capturing inter-profile interactions via a transformer yields additional gains. Why this is the best next experiment: the aggregation method is the most fundamental architectural decision in the multiprofile pipeline, and resolving it early (before exploring RNA encoder variants, image encoder variants, or fusion strategies) maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget. If transformer outperforms avgpool, it opens a new promising axis; if not, we confirm avgpool sufficiency and can redirect effort to other design dimensions.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) is the best result so far at 0.619 acc, and avgpool clearly outperforms transformer aggregation (0.619 vs 0.579). However, all multimodal results to date used concat fusion; the effect of weighted fusion is entirely untested. Question: config_019 is a single-variable change from config_018 (concat → weighted fusion), cleanly isolating whether learned modality weighting can improve upon simple concatenation in the best-performing setup. Why this is the best next experiment: it is the lowest-risk, highest-information-value exploitation of the current best configuration. If weighted fusion helps, we immediately have a better config and a new productive axis; if it does not, we rule out fusion as a lever and can confidently pivot to testing a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) or learned RNA encoder (SCVI/scGPT) in subsequent experiments, avoiding wasted budget on a dimension that does not matter.

The current best configuration (config_019: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.639) establishes that multiprofile + avgpool + weighted fusion is the strongest architecture. However, the image encoder axis is completely unexplored in the multimodal setting—we have only tested ResNet50. Config_025 swaps the image encoder to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L while holding all other settings at their proven-best values (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted, pca_n2000). This is a clean single-variable test: if ViT-L improves performance, it reveals the image modality is underutilized and opens a new optimization direction; if it does not, it confirms ResNet50 is sufficient and redirects effort toward the RNA encoder axis (scVI, scGPT). Under a limited budget, this experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about one of the two major unexplored design axes (image encoder vs. RNA encoder) while preserving all settings that have shown strong evidence of benefit.

Evidence: The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder, and all six completed experiments share this encoder. The key unexplored dimension is whether a learned RNA representation (scvi_n200) can improve upon PCA in the multimodal setting. Config_031 tests scvi_n200 while holding all other settings at their empirically best values (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion). This is the highest-information experiment because: (1) it directly addresses the largest remaining uncertainty—whether the RNA bottleneck is the encoder or something else; (2) if scvi_n200 improves, it opens a strong exploitation path; if it does not, we can rule out learned RNA encoders as a lever and focus remaining budget on other axes; (3) compared to testing transformer+weighted (config_021), which is unlikely to beat avgpool+weighted given the 4-point gap already observed with concat, the RNA encoder question has far greater potential to shift the performance landscape.

1) Evidence: The current best (config_031: SCVI+ResNet50+avgpool+weighted, acc 0.678) was achieved by upgrading the RNA encoder from PCA to SCVI (+4%). The image encoder choice (ResNet50 vs ViT) showed negligible difference under PCA (0.639 vs 0.635), but this interaction has not been tested under SCVI's richer latent representations. 2) This experiment (config_037: SCVI+ViT+avgpool+weighted) completes the 2×2 grid of RNA encoder × image encoder within the confirmed-best framework (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted), directly testing whether ViT's hierarchical features complement SCVI's learned space more effectively than ResNet50's. 3) Under a limited budget, this is the highest-value exploitation step: it is low-risk (all other components are validated winners), it could yield a new best configuration, and it definitively resolves whether the image-encoder dimension still matters once SCVI is in place—freeing future experiments to focus on the remaining unexplored RNA encoder (SCGPT) or aggregation variants.

Evidence: The current best (config_037, scvi_n200 + vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) establishes that multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion, and vit_l are strong choices, and scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000 by ~4%. However, scgpt—a fundamentally different generative RNA encoder—has never been tested in any multimodal configuration, leaving a major source of uncertainty about whether an alternative learned representation could match or exceed scvi_n200. This experiment (config_049: scgpt + vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile) isolates the RNA encoder as the single variable against the best-known settings for all other dimensions. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it reduces uncertainty on the highest-impact unexplored axis: if scgpt performs comparably, it opens a new search branch; if it underperforms significantly, it confirms scvi_n200 as the optimal encoder and lets us concentrate remaining experiments on finer-grained choices (e.g., transformer vs avgpool with scvi_n200, or concat vs weighted).

Evidence: The current best (config_037: scvi_n200, vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.706 acc. Prior experiments show avgpool outperformed transformer by ~0.06 (config_019 vs config_020, both pca_n2000/resnet50), the largest single-variable effect observed. However, this aggregation comparison was only tested with the weaker pca_n2000 encoder. Uncertainty: It is untested whether transformer aggregation might interact favorably with the richer scvi_n200 representations and the higher-dimensional vit_l features, potentially closing or reversing the gap. This experiment (config_039) is a clean single-variable swap (avgpool→transformer) from the current best, directly testing whether the aggregation preference is encoder-agnostic. If transformer is again inferior, we can confidently lock in avgpool for all remaining experiments; if it performs competitively or better, it reveals an important interaction effect that changes the design space. Under a limited budget, confirming or ruling out the aggregation choice for the top-performing encoder pair is the highest-information next step before further exploitation.
